anomaly_def.Name: SQL Workload Logic Anomaly + Transaction Lock Contention Anomaly + Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
SQL Workload Logic Anomaly: Application-level statements or transaction demarcations are written so that they scan or modify more data and hold transactions open longer than business logic truly requires.
Transaction Lock Contention Anomaly: Concurrent transactions request incompatible locks on the same rows, keys, or tables, causing blocking chains or deadlocks that stall or abort work.
Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly: Engine parameters governing memory, logging, checkpoints, parallelism, or connection limits are mis-tuned relative to hardware and workload, degrading internal subsystems without the physical resources being saturated.

When all three root causes manifest together, the database exhibits extreme and erratic latency spikes, frequent deadlock terminations, surges of lock-wait and log-write wait events, sudden freezes during checkpoint storms, and application timeouts that persist even when CPU, I/O, or memory usage appear modest. Slow, chatty, or over-broad SQL keeps transactions open long enough for lock queues to grow; mis-sized memory pools and overly aggressive checkpoint or parallelism settings magnify the time locks are held and lengthen recovery after deadlock rollbacks. Administrators may observe fluctuating throughput, bloated lock tables, escalating connection-pool backlogs, and oscillations between underutilized and saturated hardware states that defy single-factor explanations.

Causally, inefficient workload logic inflates read and update footprints, extending transaction duration and expanding the scope of acquired locks. These enlarged lock footprints collide under high concurrency, giving rise to intense blocking and deadlocks. Simultaneously, sub-optimal configuration—such as too small a buffer pool, low lock-table memory, or tight checkpoint intervals—slows I/O, increases page latch times, and prolongs lock retention during physical writes or rollback processing. The misconfiguration therefore amplifies the delays introduced by poor SQL logic, while the swelling lock contention further stresses memory and logging subsystems already constrained by bad parameter choices, creating a feedback loop that degrades OLTP performance severely and obscures individual root-cause signals.

entry.official_definition: The number of seconds to wait for more data from a source/replica connection before aborting the read.
entry.trigger_condition: A replica waits longer than replica_net_timeout for more data from the source connection.
entry.workload_impact: The replication network read is aborted and the replica considers the connection interrupted.
entry.default_behavior: Defined as a MySQL replication system variable.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when connection establishment, authentication exchange, or session activity does not progress within the allowed time budget.
entry.solution_guidance: Check connection lifecycle, client responsiveness, authentication latency, idle-session handling, and whether connection pools are holding stale sessions.
